objective.statement: Choose suitable chords for the melody notes at a cadence point.
successCriteria: I list the chords that contain each melody note.
I find a pair that makes the cadence asked for.
I know several pairs may be correct.

explanation.text: In the examination you may be shown a short melody in C, G, D or F major, with letters A, B and so on above the notes that need chords. You do not have to harmonise the whole melody. At each marked note you choose a chord that contains the note, and the chords must make the cadence the question names. You may name the chords by Roman numerals, by letter names, or by writing notes on the staves.

Work in two steps. First, for each marked note, list every chord of I, ii, IV and V that contains it. In C major the melody note C is in chord I (C E G) and chord IV (F A C); the note D is in chord ii (D F A) and chord V (G B D). Look at the notes of each chord to make your list.

music.textAlternative: The notes of the four chords of C major: I (C E G), ii (D F A), IV (F A C), V (G B D).

explanation.caption: The four chords you may choose from in C major.

explanation.text: Second, look for a pair that makes the cadence. If the cadence is perfect, you need V then I. If it is plagal, IV then I. If it is imperfect, the second chord is V and the first is I, ii or IV. A note such as G fits I and V, so both V–I and I–V can be made: check which cadence the question wants. There is often more than one correct pair.
List the chords that contain each melody note, then pick a pair that makes the named cadence. Any valid pair is correct.

music.textAlternative: Two chords in C major: V then I.

steps: D is in V (G B D); C is in I (C E G).
V followed by I: a perfect cadence.

mastery.completion: The lesson is complete when every step has been answered correctly (retries allowed). Only first-attempt, hint-free independent answers count as mastery evidence; guided steps never do.

provenance.authoredBy: Music Theory Path curriculum team (Brief 05, drafted with AI assistance; pending qualified teacher review)
provenance.notes: Original wording and melodies. First Steps Grade 5 section 11 (pp. 122-126, read in the PDF): chords suggested at indicated cadence points in C, G, D or F; Roman numerals, letter names or written notes; no penalty for poor spacing. Every pair of chords that contains the melody notes and makes the named cadence is accepted (no single 'right' sequence).
